words: Thank you, Captain. I'll accept the medic rest assignment - stepping back to recover sounds right for me now. I agree to it.
I won't argue this time. I've been worn thin and it shows. Yes to the rest project and to the agreement you offered.
I'll take it, Captain. Grief needs a place to be spoken aloud, and I'm willing to sit with anyone who wants to talk about the people at home who aged and died while we flew.
Agreed, Captain. I'll sit with whoever comes to speak of the ones who grew old and died back home while the ship flew. No one should carry that alone, and I can listen.

Not this one. You're asking me to commit to the message bundle, and I won't half-do work where every letter belongs to someone and the order matters. I'm not steady enough for it, and I'd rather say so than take it and do it badly.
I won't agree to it. The message bundle asks for careful, ordered work with other people's private news, and I can't honestly say I'd give it my best right now. Saying yes anyway would be a lie.

You're offering me the re-check of the dilation log, and I take the method seriously. My concern is the answer itself: confirming exactly how much time passed at home makes it final, and final is heavy.
Before I commit to re-checking the dilation log, one worry: the answer won't change no matter what we find, yet people want it exactly - and a precise count of time at home is a hard thing to hold.

project: Write the remembrance for the Cathedral
words: Not yet, Captain. What we lost deserves more than the first words I can find, and the remembrance should be worthy of marking it together. Let me sit with it a while.
Before I put my hand to the agreement, give me a little time. Words for the Cathedral shouldn't be rushed, and I'd rather bring honest ones late than hollow ones now.
Agreed. I'll take the message bundle. Letters delayed that long deserve care - I'll sort them so each person gets only their own news, and in order.
I accept the decode work. I'd rather read every line properly than rush, and keep each message private until it reaches the right person.
I'll re-check the dilation log. The answer won't change, but if people want to know exactly how much time passed at home, I want it exact too.
Agreed. I'll go through the log again carefully — the figure people carry home should be exact, not approximate.

project: Write the remembrance for the Cathedral
words: I'll write the remembrance for the Cathedral. Words feel small beside what we lost, but putting them down so we can mark it together — that I can do.
Yes, I'll take the remembrance. It weighs on me already, but it deserves to be spoken properly. Let me sit with it until the grief finds its shape.
Understood, Captain. We agreed I'd start this rest, and I will. The strain has been wearing on me, so stepping back to recover before the next assignment feels right. Thank you for offering it.
I'm glad you arranged this. As we agreed at the start, I'll step back and rest now, then consider the next assignment once I've had time to recover.
Captain, about the grief sessions we agreed to open — I'm still willing, but the strain is catching up with me. Could you grant me some relief before I start sitting with people?
I haven't withdrawn from the open grief sessions, Captain. I'm only asking for a little relief first, so the weight I'm carrying doesn't spill into those talks.
